steps.note: S1.3.1.1 states that for arbitrary initial scratch vectors a,c the schedule changes the targets by (JV+RG)x independently of a,c and restores the scratch wires, and the S1.3.1 method gives the subtract-first, undo-last order; the quote at line 748 is used in the paper's role.
S1.3.1.2 states the central coefficient |S∩T| mod 2, that the side wires cancel exactly the intersection-one pairs, and that the self coefficient is one, which matches the paper.
The plan treats only the bit construction; nowhere does it state the complex central coefficient (|S∩T|-1)/2 or that the side wires cancel intersections zero and two.
S1.3.1.3 gives the three stages (x,y)->(x,y+x)->(-y,y+x)->(-y,x), with each invocation restoring its own scratch wires, as in the paper.

S1.3.3.5 claims that every edge joins comparable labels and its method says to tabulate the residuals by splitting A=B⊥P and F=<t>⊥t^⊥, but the plan never gives the table's per-edge residuals and dimensions (only the side 2->5 and center 3->4 entries appear), so it names the table without its content.
S1.3.3.5.1 states the inclusion (B⊗F)⊥(P⊗<t_X>) ⊂ (B⊗F)⊥(P⊗t_Y^⊥) because t_X⊥t_Y, with residual P⊗<t_X,t_Y>^⊥ of dimension h-2.

The plan states that the only decreasing edge is center 3->4 (losing h), that sources sum to N and sinks to W_b m-N, that the signed changes telescope to W_b m-2N, and that the Ic losses add 2L to give the absolute total W_b m-2N+2L.

S2.1.1 states that over F_2 every nonzero residual is nondegenerate and contains a norm-one vector, so it is nonalternating and has an orthonormal basis; it does not spell out the plane-absorption proof that the paper gives 'for completeness'.
S2.1.2 gives the weight identity, additivity mod 4 on orthogonal vectors, and q_V-q_U = Σ_v wt(v)[v·x] mod 4 over an orthonormal basis of the residual.

S2.1.3 states that wt(v) is odd, so the phase is i^{ε[v·x]} = (1+i^ε)/2+(1-i^ε)/2(-1)^{v·x}, and that Hadamard conjugation turns (-1)^{v·x} into X_v, which gives aI+bX_v or its inverse; this is a faithful paraphrase of H diag(1,-1) H = X.

S2.1 gives one kernel per residual-basis vector, s_c in all, and S2.3 (with its quote at line 1905, where the paper uses this count) states the multi-column form: summing residual dimensions gives exactly s_c child calls, each a C^{⊗f} layer on the f axes of one slot.

S2.1.5 states the zero-label frame I and the full-label frame C^{⊗m}, C^{-1} on the 27 coordinates of supp(u_a) on the X_a route, and the repair by Z signs before and i^{27k} after, using C=iZC^{-1}Z (from the S2.1 method); it omits the Z after the network and the final negation of the X outputs.
S1.3.3.6 and S1.3.3.7.3 give L_b<N/2, hence s_b = W_b m-N+2L_b falls short of W_b m by N-2L_b>0, and S2.1.4 gives the complex deficit 2N-2L_c>0 from L_c/N<1/2.
The plan never states η_c = 73/19906842167500; S2.8 only asserts s_c/W_c ≤ m^σ.

S1.3.3.8 gives the mechanism: the deficit exceeds 20·2^{-50} and log m<20, so m^{1-2^{-50}} > m(1-20·2^{-50}) > m(1-η) and s/W<m^τ with τ=1-2^{-50}; its quote covers both deficits and S4.4.1 sets τ=σ, though the complex instance is only asserted.

S1.3.4.1 describes elimination with the topmost nonzero row's rightmost entry as pivot, using only lower-triangular operations, which gives A=E_1ΠE_2 with exactly a ones; the repetition on the active indices is carried by the quote at line 1389.
S1.3.4.2 states a fixed odd prime avoiding every denominator and diagonal numerator in the finite table of factors, so the identities specialize to Z/q^b with invertible triangular factors.
S1.3.4.3 states that a lower-triangular change updates the m coordinates in descending physical order by controlled shifts from earlier fields, at cost O(V).
S1.3.4.4 gives D_j<-D_j+H_i, the interchange, then D_j<-H_i-D_j, which yields (h+d,d) with one interchange, hence a interchanges in all.
The plan mentions only Δ=⌈C_0 d^{C_1}⌉ (S2.9) and εC_1<1 (S4.4.1); it never defines E=64(W+m+1)^3, B=s+E, ν, C_1=max{20,ν+3} or C_0=128mB^2, and never gives the values ν=11, C_1=20.
The arithmetic-depth recurrence A(e) ≤ sA(e/m)+E with A(e) ≤ 8e at a leaf, and the per-invocation count below E, appear nowhere in the plan; S2.9 only asserts depth Δ=o(p).
The plan never unrolls the depth recurrence (B^{k+1} ≤ B^2 d^ν, A(e) ≤ 8B^2 d^{ν+1}, total below C_0 d^{C_1}).

S2.9 asserts that p+Δ fractional and Δ+3 integer bits are exact and that Δ=o(p), but it omits the core induction (a value at depth ℓ lies in 2^{-(p+ℓ)}Z[i] with modulus at most 2^ℓ) and never ties εC_1<1 to Δ=o(p).
S2.10 states that every row of H has absolute row sum one, so disks map to disks, and that the final truncation errs by less than √2·2^{-p}.

summary: P02 states the bit-case bank exchange (B1, B2, B4), most of the label budget (L2-L5), the whole phase interface (P1-P4), the rank deficits except η_c (R1, R2, R4), the whole matrix shear (M1-M4) and the disk-preservation step S5: 19 of 26 present. Absent: the complex exchange coefficient (B3); the residual table itself (L1, named but not given); η_c (R3); and the guard-width derivation (S1-S4), which the plan reduces to the asserted Δ=⌈C_0 d^{C_1}⌉=o(p) and the bit reservation. No sub-step is stated contrary to the paper.
